revision_reasoning: The pedestrian swing gate is the only proposed package that meets the target of 10 conflicts per 1,000 under nominal conditions (6.7) and stays well under the limit in two of three stress tests (6.7 when the mirror is ignored, 13.5 during night-shift inattention). However, it degrades to 22.7 when gate compliance drops to 60%, exceeding the target. The other two proposals exceed the target even nominally (19.3 and 25.3) and worsen significantly under stress (up to 52.1 and 61.7). No tested package satisfies the target across all stress scenarios. A new package that combines the gate with a warning light directly addresses the gate-compliance weakness: the light alerts pedestrians even if they bypass the gate, and the single-control test shows the light alone yields 27.4 conflicts, suggesting the combination can close the gap. A second new package adds the warning light to the moved-crossing-plus-mirror-plus-sign bundle, which already reaches 19.3 nominally; the light's strong alert effect (95%) should pull it below 10 and improve night-shift resilience where that bundle hit 52.1.
